findings.title: Daily sales report filters by show_date, not by the date the sale was made
findings.spec_item: Daily sales report DOWNLOAD: date, total bookings, per island, per channel, AND time-of-day breakdown
findings.current_state: Both the CSV route (.eq("show_date", date) at daily-sales.csv/route.ts:32) and the on-screen Daily sales tab (lists/page.tsx:21-26 builds the same show_date query; byHour at lists/page.tsx:67-72) select bookings whose SHOW is on the chosen date, then bucket them by created_at hour. A 'daily sales report' is bookings TAKEN that day (any show date). As built, the report mixes creation times from many different days into one 'time-of-day' breakdown (meaningless), and bookings sold today for future shows never appear on today's report. Joel cannot answer 'what did we sell today and when' — the core purpose of the report.
findings.fix: Filter on created_at within the selected date (in the business's local timezone), across all show dates; optionally keep a second 'show night' view. The time-of-day breakdown then becomes coherent. Add revenue and pax totals to the summary section while there (currently counts only, route.ts:54-62).
findings.verify_note: route.ts:32 .eq("show_date", date) and lists/page.tsx:25 both filter on show_date, then bucket created_at UTC hours (route.ts:48-51, page.tsx:70-71). Grep across the entire show-ops module finds NO created_at-based sales query anywhere — no alternate implementation exists. Sales made today for future show dates never appear; the time-of-day histogram mixes creation times from many different days. Summary is counts-only (route.ts:54-62), no revenue/pax. Blocker severity is fair: the report answers the wrong question entirely. Bonus defect: getUTCHours is off by one for Canary local time (UTC+1 in summer).

findings.title: Office list is not 'per show' — all shows on a date are merged into one table with no show grouping or filter
findings.spec_item: Office list per show: arranged ALPHABETICAL by supplier then by surname
findings.current_state: The office sort (lists/page.tsx:34-38) is supplier→surname across ALL bookings for the date (island filter optional); show is just a column. If two shows run the same night (e.g. two islands, or two shows on one island) the office gets one interleaved list. The DateIslandFilter component already supports includeShow/showNames (date-island-filter.tsx props) but lists/page.tsx never passes includeShow, so you cannot even filter to a single show. Supplier-then-surname sort itself is correct: surnameKey takes the LAST whitespace token (calc.ts:59-62), not the first word.
findings.fix: Group the office list into one section (and one print page-break) per show_name, each independently sorted supplier→surname; pass includeShow + showNames to DateIslandFilter on the lists page.
findings.verify_note: lists/page.tsx:34-38 sorts supplier→surname across ALL bookings for the date; show is just a column (line 159), no per-show sections or print page-breaks. DateIslandFilter supports includeShow/showNames (date-island-filter.tsx:11-14,77-93) and payments/page.tsx:88-90 proves it works, but lists/page.tsx never passes it and its searchParams type (line 9) accepts no show param at all. surnameKey correctly uses last name token (calc.ts:59-62). Partial mitigation: the island filter isolates a show when only one show runs per island-night, but spec's 'per show' is not met and same-island multi-show nights interleave.

findings.title: Bus list has no per-stop pax subtotals and no total-on-board figure
findings.spec_item: Bus lists: by date → island → resort, in stop-time order, for bus guides incl. info they need (per-stop pax)
findings.current_state: The bus tab (lists/page.tsx:176-191) renders one flat row per booking with per-booking pax. There are no subtotal rows per stop, per resort, or per island, and no grand total, so a guide must mentally sum pax at each pick-up and for the whole bus. Sort order itself is correct per spec: island→resort→stop sort_order→time (lists/page.tsx:53-60), guide_notes are included (line 187).
findings.fix: Group rows under island/resort/stop headings with a pax subtotal per stop and a total pax for the bus; keep the existing sort keys.
findings.verify_note: Facts fully confirmed: lists/page.tsx:176-191 renders flat per-booking rows via ListTable (243-278) which has no subtotal or grand-total mechanism; sort (53-60) and guide_notes (187) are correct as conceded. However 'per-stop pax' is the auditor's inference — Joel's spec literally says only 'incl. info they need'. Reclassify as a UX/completeness defect against the 'flawless' bar rather than a hard spec violation; severity major is defensible for a nightly printed guide sheet (guide must hand-sum pax per stop and on-board total) but minor is arguable.

findings.title: Outlook: direct (non-bus) bookings are grouped by hotel name instead of resort
findings.spec_item: Weekly outlook: per resort: pax-direct vs pax-bus
findings.current_state: Resort is resolved only via pickup_stop_id (outlook/page.tsx:64-68). Direct bookings have no pickup stop, so they fall back to raw hotel_name (or 'Direct / unknown'). Result: the same resort appears multiple times — once as the real resort for bus pax, plus one row per hotel for direct pax — so the 'per resort direct vs bus' comparison the spec asks for never lines up. The data to fix it exists: bookings carry hotel_id, show_hotels maps hotel→bus_stop_id, and stops carry resort, but the page never queries show_hotels.
findings.fix: Fetch show_hotels for the island, map hotel_id → bus_stop_id → resort, and use that as the resort key for non-transport bookings (falling back to hotel name only when unmapped).
findings.verify_note: outlook/page.tsx:64-68 resolves resort only via pickup_stop_id (fallback: pickup_stop_name split, hotel_name, 'Direct / unknown'). Both creation paths set pickup_stop_id only when transport && hotel.bus_stop_id (actions.ts:348-359, brain-tools.ts:235-246), so every direct booking falls through to hotel_name. The page queries only products/bookings/bus orders/stops (lines 14-47) — show_hotels (which carries bus_stop_id, per migration 20260811120000_show_ops.sql) is never fetched, though stops carry resort. Spec's per-resort direct-vs-bus rows therefore fragment: one resort row for bus pax plus one row per hotel for direct pax.

findings.title: Ops Brain-created bookings hardcode sales_channel to 'direct', silently corrupting the sales-report channel breakdown
findings.spec_item: Daily sales report broken down by channel (tour op / direct sales / partner hotels-shops-agencies); non-functional: everything automated, no manual cross-inputting
findings.current_state: brain-tools.ts:293 sets sales_channel: "direct" on every booking created through the Ops Brain chat, even when a supplier (tour op / hotel / agency) is attached. The manual form is only slightly better: actions.ts:395-397 takes a hand-picked channel defaulting to "direct" and never cross-checks it against the chosen supplier's partner_type. Any misfiled booking permanently skews the daily sales by-channel figures (route.ts:47) that Joel will use commercially. There is also no rollup of hotel/shop/agency into the spec's 'partner' group, though the finer granularity is arguably a superset.
findings.fix: Derive sales_channel automatically from the supplier's partner_type when a supplier is set (direct only when supplier is null), in both brain-tools.ts and actions.ts; optionally emit the three spec groups (tour op / direct / partner) as a rollup section in the CSV.
findings.verify_note: brain-tools.ts:293 hardcodes sales_channel:"direct" even when supplier_id/supplier_name are attached (lines 278-279). Manual form: actions.ts:395-397 accepts any configured channel defaulting 'direct'; booking-form.tsx:423-436 is an uncontrolled select with zero linkage to the supplier field. Impact is WIDER than claimed: besides the CSV by_channel (route.ts:47), reports/page.tsx:62-63 computes the on-screen 'tour-op vs direct' tile from sales_channel, while the same page's per-partner-type sections (lines 55,94) derive from supplier partner_type — an internal inconsistency where the two views of the same data disagree. No tour-op/direct/partner rollup exists (default channel list at types.ts:61 is finer-grained).

findings.title: Outlook bus spaces are computed per show but bus orders exist per island-night — seats double-counted when two shows share a night, and individual buses per show can't be recorded
findings.spec_item: Buses: which bus ordered per show + size + cost; outlook bus spaces remaining
findings.current_state: Nights are keyed `${show_date}|${show_name}` (outlook/page.tsx:58) but busByDate is keyed by date alone (line 77) and the DB enforces unique (business_id, show_date, island) on show_bus_orders (supabase/migrations/20260811120000_show_ops.sql:162-171, upsert onConflict at actions.ts:312-314). So (a) two shows on the same island-night each show the FULL seats_ordered against only their own bus pax — combined 'spaces left' overstates capacity; (b) Joel's master-data spec is per SHOW per bus, and multiple physical buses for one night must be manually summed into a single row (master/page.tsx:380-397 offers only one seats/cost pair per island-date). Note the DB constraint does prevent the naive Map-collision bug — one order per island-date is all that can exist.
findings.fix: Either key bus orders by show (add product_id/show_name to show_bus_orders and to the outlook join) or, at minimum, compute spaces at island-night level (seats_ordered minus bus pax summed across ALL shows that night) and show it once per night. Allow multiple bus rows per night (drop the unique constraint, sum seats/cost) to record individual buses as spec'd.
findings.verify_note: Nights keyed `${show_date}|${show_name}` (outlook/page.tsx:58); busByDate keyed by date alone (line 77); spaces = seats_ordered minus THAT show's bus pax only (lines 104-106), so two shows on one island-night each display the full order and combined spaces-left overstates capacity. unique (business_id, show_date, island) confirmed in migration 20260811120000_show_ops.sql show_bus_orders DDL, matching upsert onConflict actions.ts:312-314; master/page.tsx:380-397 offers exactly one seats/cost pair per island-date and no later migration alters the table. Spec's 'which bus ordered per show + size + cost' (and multiple physical buses per night) cannot be represented. Double-count only manifests when an island runs two shows the same night, but the modelling gap vs spec is real regardless.

findings.title: Outlook 'next 5 show nights' only sees nights that already have bookings, within a hard 21-day window
findings.spec_item: Weekly outlook: next 5 show nights
findings.current_state: Show nights are derived solely from existing bookings in today..today+21d (outlook/page.tsx:22-34, 57-76; the comment on line 21 stale-ly says 14 days). A show night with a bus already ordered but zero bookings yet is invisible, and a weekly-frequency show yields at most 3 of the promised 5 nights. There is no show-schedule source of truth (show_products has no schedule), so the page can genuinely say 'No upcoming bookings' while buses are on order.
findings.fix: Union night keys from show_bus_orders (and any future show schedule) with booking-derived nights so zero-booking nights render with 0 pax and full spaces; widen or remove the 21-day cap so 5 nights are always found; fix the stale comment.

findings.title: Outlook clamps 'spaces left' at 0, hiding bus overbooking
findings.spec_item: flawless-system
findings.current_state: spaces = Math.max(0, order.seats_ordered - busPax) (outlook/page.tsx:106). If 55 bus pax are booked against a 50-seat order, the page shows 'spaces left 0' — indistinguishable from exactly full — instead of warning that 5 guests have no seat. For an ops screen whose whole job is bus capacity, this hides the one state that needs action.
findings.fix: Show the negative overage explicitly (e.g. 'OVERBOOKED by 5' in red) instead of clamping to zero.

findings.title: Infants are counted as full bus-seat occupants in spaces-left math — needs confirming with Joel
findings.spec_item: Weekly outlook: bus spaces remaining (infants counting)
findings.current_state: paxTotal = adults + children + infants (calc.ts:70-72) and the outlook adds that full figure to bus pax (outlook/page.tsx:70-71), so a lap infant consumes a bus seat in spaces-left. On Spanish coaches with seatbelts every occupant needs a seat, so this may be correct — but if MHT treats lap infants as seatless, spaces-left is systematically understated. Same total is used for the Pax column on office/bus lists (lists/page.tsx:161,185) with no adults/children/infants split shown anywhere on the lists.
findings.fix: Confirm the seat rule with Joel; if lap infants don't take seats, exclude (or separately annotate) infants in the bus-spaces calculation, and show the A/C/I split on office and bus lists rather than a single Pax number.

findings.title: All dates and the time-of-day breakdown use UTC, not Canary/UK local time
findings.spec_item: Daily sales time-of-day breakdown; flawless-system
findings.current_state: Hour buckets use getUTCHours (route.ts:48-50; lists/page.tsx:70, labelled 'UTC hour'), and 'today' defaults come from new Date().toISOString() (route.ts:23; lists/page.tsx:17; outlook/page.tsx:12). Canary Islands run UTC+1 in summer and the UK tour is on BST, so every summer sale is bucketed an hour early and, between 00:00-01:00 local, the default date is yesterday. A UK-tour winter/summer mix also shifts.
findings.fix: Store or configure a tenant timezone (e.g. Atlantic/Canary) in ShowOpsConfig and convert created_at to it for hour buckets and for the default 'today' date.

findings.title: Bus list sorts by the stop's CURRENT pickup time but displays the booking's SNAPSHOT time
findings.spec_item: Bus lists in stop-time order
findings.current_state: time_key prefers stop?.pickup_time (live master data) over b.pickup_time (lists/page.tsx:49), but the rendered Time column prints b.pickup_time — the value frozen at booking time (line 181). If Joel edits a stop's pickup time after bookings exist, the printed list shows stale times while sorting by the new ones, so a guide can see out-of-order or simply wrong times on the sheet.
findings.fix: Render the same resolved time used for sorting (stop.pickup_time ?? b.pickup_time), and consider flagging bookings whose snapshot differs from the current stop time so the office knows to re-notify guests.

findings.title: Wide office/bus list tables are truncated in browser print; no proper PDF output
findings.spec_item: Daily outputs print quality; flawless-system
findings.current_state: Printing is browser-print only ('Use your browser Print for PDF', lists/page.tsx:133-136 — and there is no Print button, just the hint). ListTable wraps every table in overflow-x-auto with no print override (line 245), so an office list with several custom-question columns, or the 8-column bus list, gets clipped at the paper edge when it overflows — the hidden columns simply don't print. There is also no per-show/per-section page-break control. Branded print header does exist (lines 103-119), which is good.
findings.fix: Add print CSS: overflow-visible + table-layout/font-size shrink for print, break-inside-avoid per section and break-before per show group; add a visible Print button; longer-term generate a real PDF (e.g. @react-pdf or Puppeteer route) for guide/office handouts.

findings.title: Office list omits the booking reference
findings.spec_item: Office list: includes all info office needs incl. ticket # and comments
findings.current_state: Office list columns are Supplier, Guest, Show, Hotel, Pax, Ticket #, custom questions, Comments (lists/page.tsx:141-171). The auto-generated MHT booking_ref — the primary key the office quotes on the phone and matches against supplier tickets and invoices — is not a column, and neither is any transport/pickup indicator or dietary flag, so the office cannot cross-reference or spot bus guests from this sheet alone. Ticket # and office_comments ARE present, and office_only_comments is correctly kept off all printed lists.
findings.fix: Add booking_ref as the first column; consider compact Transport (Y/N + stop) and Dietary (Y) indicator columns.

findings.title: CSV cells are not hardened against spreadsheet formula injection
findings.spec_item: flawless-system
findings.current_state: csvCell (route.ts:6-9) quotes commas/quotes/newlines but does not neutralise cells beginning with =, +, -, or @. Guest names, hotel names and supplier ticket numbers are operator- or brain-entered free text; a value like '=HYPERLINK(...)' or '+1234' executes/mangles when the office opens the download in Excel — the exact consumption path this file is built for.
findings.fix: Prefix cells starting with =, +, -, @ (and tab/CR) with a single quote, and quote fields containing \r as well.

findings.title: CSV route skips the lists-module plan gate that the lists page enforces
findings.spec_item: flawless-system
findings.current_state: lists/page.tsx:13-15 blocks tenants without the 'lists' module (hasShowOpsModule), but the CSV route only checks auth + show_ops_enabled (route.ts:16-21) — it never loads config/tier or calls hasShowOpsModule, and applies no role floor. Any member of any show-ops-enabled workspace (starter tier included, booker role included) can pull the full financial detail CSV directly by URL even when the UI says 'Lists module not on your plan'.
findings.fix: In the route, load the business config + tier and enforce hasShowOpsModule(config, tier, 'lists') (and a role floor if lists are meant to be office+), mirroring the page.

findings.title: surnameKey mis-sorts 'Surname, First' entries and suffixed names
findings.spec_item: Office list arranged alphabetical by supplier then by surname
findings.current_state: surnameKey takes the last whitespace token (calc.ts:59-62), which correctly avoids the first-word trap for 'John Smith'. But 'Smith, John' sorts under J, 'John Smith Jr' sorts under 'jr', and multi-part surnames rely on the last token only. Tour-op manifests commonly arrive surname-first, so comma-format entries are likely in real data.
findings.fix: If the name contains a comma, use the text before the comma as the surname key; strip common suffixes (Jr/Sr/II/III) before taking the last token.

findings.title: Dietary list has no pax/party-size column
findings.spec_item: Dietary list
findings.current_state: Dietary tab shows Guest, Show, Hotel, Notes only (lists/page.tsx:193-198). The kitchen can't see whether 'gluten free' applies to a party of 2 or 9, or how many total covers the note sits inside, without cross-referencing the office list.
findings.fix: Add a Pax column (and ideally the A/C/I split) to the dietary list rows.

findings.title: Daily sales summary lacks revenue and pax totals
findings.spec_item: Daily sales report DOWNLOAD (flawless-system)
findings.current_state: The summary section (route.ts:54-62) and the on-screen sales tab (lists/page.tsx:201-230) report booking COUNTS only — no revenue total, no pax total, per island or per channel — even though total_cost and pax fields are already selected into the detail rows. Joel's literal spec asks for booking counts, but a daily sales report he'll run the business on needs the money line.
findings.fix: Add total_revenue and total_pax to the summary, and revenue/pax columns to the by_island and by_channel breakdown lines.

findings.title: Deposit/balance bookkeeping is self-contradictory — bookings never 'clear as we do' and recording a payment can INCREASE the displayed balance
findings.spec_item: Payments tab: deposits due, manually enter cash/card, clears live as entered
findings.current_state: At booking creation, calc.ts:47 sets balance_remaining = total − deposit_amount (e.g. total €100, 30% deposit → balance €70 with ZERO payments recorded). But every recomputation uses the other semantic: paymentStatusAfter (calc.ts:89-98) and recordPaymentAction (actions.ts:598-601) and applyShowOpsStripePayment (apply-payment.ts:46-49) set balance = total_cost − sum(payments). Concrete failure: booking €100/€30 deposit shows balance €70; office records the guest's €70 door payment (the pre-filled default at payments/page.tsx:116) → paid=70, balance recalcs to 100−70=€30, payment_status='partial' — the booking stays on the Payments-due list forever (page filters neq payment_status 'paid', payments/page.tsx:45) and its balance flips from 70 to 30. Worse: record a €5 part-payment and the balance jumps 70→95 on screen. The system never decides whether the agent-held deposit counts as collected money, so Joel's core 'clears live as entered' flow is broken for the standard deposit booking.
findings.fix: Pick one semantic and enforce it everywhere. If the partner-held deposit counts as collected (guest only owes the balance): make paymentStatusAfter take deposit_amount and compute balance = total − deposit − paid, so paying the shown balance sets status 'paid'. If instead all money must flow through the system: set initial balance_remaining = total_cost in computeBookingMoney and show 'deposit due €X / balance due €Y' as separate figures. Add a regression test for the €100/30% case.
findings.verify_note: Verified at every cited site. calc.ts:47 sets initial balance_remaining = total − deposit (€100/30% → 70 with zero payment rows; createBookingAction inserts no payment). Every recomputation uses balance = total − sum(payments): calc.ts:94-96 (paymentStatusAfter), actions.ts:598-601 (recordPaymentAction), actions.ts:497-500 (updateBookingAction), apply-payment.ts:46-49 (Stripe webhook). Math checks out: record the prefilled €70 (payments/page.tsx:116) → paid=70, balance=30, status 'partial'; booking never leaves the Payments-due list (filter .neq('payment_status','paid') at payments/page.tsx:45). Record €5 → balance display jumps 70→95. Searched the whole module for any code that records the deposit as a payment or subtracts deposit_amount in the recompute — none exists. Blocker severity is fair: this is the core 'clears live as entered' flow and every standard deposit booking hits it.

findings.title: Payments-due prefill and emailed Stripe link charge the wrong amount for unpaid deposit bookings
findings.spec_item: Payments tab: deposits due + Matty's Stripe payment links
findings.current_state: defaultValue={b.balance_remaining || b.deposit_amount}: for an unpaid deposit booking balance_remaining (total − deposit) is non-zero, so the deposit_amount fallback is dead code — the office is pre-filled with the full balance when the thing due is the deposit. Identical logic drives the emailed Stripe link amount at actions.ts:646 (due = balance_remaining > 0 ? balance_remaining : deposit_amount), and deposit-checkout.ts:52 hardcodes the description 'Balance for …' even when the intent is a deposit. A guest emailed a 'deposit' link is asked to pay the balance figure, and after paying it the booking lands in 'partial' (see the balance-semantics blocker), so they can be chased again.
findings.fix: Derive the amount from state: if no payments recorded yet, prefill/charge deposit_amount and label it 'Deposit'; once deposit is covered, prefill the true outstanding remainder and label it 'Balance'. Fix the Stripe product description to match. Depends on resolving the balance-semantics blocker first.
findings.verify_note: All code facts confirmed: payments/page.tsx:116 defaultValue={b.balance_remaining || b.deposit_amount} (fallback effectively dead since balance_remaining starts at total−deposit > 0); actions.ts:646 identical ternary drives the emailed Stripe amount; deposit-checkout.ts:52 hardcodes description 'Balance for …' on a checkout whose metadata is solvio_kind 'show_ops_deposit' (deposit-checkout.ts:64); after paying, webhook leaves status 'partial' so the guest can be chased again. ADJUSTMENT: 'wrong amount' is conditional on the unresolved semantics in the blocker above. If the deposit is partner-held and the office only ever collects the door balance (a plausible reading of Joel's model), prefilling/charging balance_remaining is the RIGHT amount and the defect collapses into the status-never-clears blocker. It is unambiguously wrong only for the flow where the office must collect the deposit itself (direct sales / phone bookings) — there is no way to charge deposit_amount at all. The dead fallback and the 'Balance' label on deposit-kind checkouts are real defects either way. Treat as a surface of the same root cause; severity major only for the deposit-collection flow.

findings.title: Editing a booking after it has been invoiced is allowed with no lock or warning — invoice and bookings silently diverge
findings.spec_item: Reservations→Invoice (CRUCIAL)
findings.current_state: updateBookingAction selects existing.invoice_id (actions.ts:484) but never checks it. After a supplier invoice pack is generated, anyone can edit the booking's pax, product, supplier or date; nett_total/adult_nett_total/child_nett_total are recomputed on the booking while show_invoice_lines and show_invoices.total_amount stay frozen at the old figures — the issued Verifactu-numbered invoice no longer matches the underlying reservations and nothing flags it. Mode flips are also unguarded: editing so billing_mode goes invoice→deposit sets payment_status 'unpaid' (actions.ts:501-505) and the guest gets chased for money the supplier is simultaneously being invoiced for; deposit→invoice after cash payments were recorded leads to the supplier being invoiced full nett on a booking that already took cash (generateInvoicePackAction filters only billing_mode+invoice_id, actions.ts:695-704, ignoring payments). The edit page (bookings/[id]/page.tsx) gives no indication the booking is on an invoice.
findings.fix: In updateBookingAction, if existing.invoice_id is set: block changes to supplier, pax, product and money fields (allow only comments/dietary/hotel-type fields), returning 'This booking is on invoice X — void the invoice first.' Show an 'Invoiced on pack #…' banner with a link on the edit page. Separately guard billing-mode flips when payments exist.
findings.verify_note: Verified. actions.ts:484 selects invoice_id but no code path checks it; the update at actions.ts:507-516 rewrites pax/product/supplier/nett fields (buildBookingFields returns nett_total etc. at 437-439) while show_invoice_lines and show_invoices.total_amount are never recomputed anywhere in the repo. Grep of bookings/[id]/page.tsx finds zero references to invoice_id/invoiced/disabled — no banner, no lock. Mode-flip paths verified: invoice→deposit hits actions.ts:496-500 → status 'unpaid' with full balance even while the booking sits on a supplier invoice (payments page doesn't filter invoice_id); deposit→invoice hits 501-504 (status 'n_a', balance 0) and generateInvoicePackAction (695-704) filters only billing_mode+invoice_id+date, ignoring show_booking_payments, so recorded cash is double-billed to the supplier. Aggravating fact the auditor missed: updateBookingAction is gated only by requireShowOpsContext (actions.ts:478) — no role check, so even a 'booker' can mutate invoiced bookings. Blocker is fair for Verifactu-numbered finance data.

findings.title: No way to void, delete or regenerate an invoice — mistakes are permanent and their bookings are locked out of future packs
findings.spec_item: Reservations→Invoice (CRUCIAL) / flawless-system
findings.current_state: The only invoice actions are generateInvoicePackAction, markInvoicePaidAction (actions.ts:762-774) and updateInvoiceMetaAction (actions.ts:776-796). There is no void/delete/un-invoice action and no un-mark-paid. If a pack is generated with the wrong period, island or supplier data, the invoice exists forever, and every booking in it has invoice_id set so it can never appear in another pack (generateInvoicePackAction filters .is('invoice_id', null), actions.ts:701) — the only recovery is direct DB surgery on a live client's finance data. Mis-ticking 'Mark paid' is likewise irreversible in the UI.
findings.fix: Add a finance/admin-only voidInvoiceAction: set a voided flag (keep the row for audit), null out invoice_id on its bookings, and exclude voided invoices from list/overdue. Add an unmark-paid action. Schema already cascades lines and sets bookings' invoice_id null on delete (migration 20260811120000_show_ops.sql:281,298), so a soft-void is straightforward.
findings.verify_note: Verified. The only invoice actions in the module are generateInvoicePackAction (actions.ts:681), markInvoicePaidAction (762) and updateInvoiceMetaAction (776); repo-wide grep shows the only .delete() in show-ops is removeShowOpsMemberAction (actions.ts:563). invoices/[id]/page.tsx is print + mark-paid only. Bookings in a pack have invoice_id set and generateInvoicePackAction filters .is('invoice_id', null) (actions.ts:701), so they can never re-enter a pack. Additional confirmed detail: once paid=true the mark-paid form is hidden (invoices/page.tsx:364) and no action can unset paid or correct paid_at — updateInvoiceMetaAction touches only verifactu/date/terms. Migration citations check out: show_invoice_lines.invoice_id on delete cascade and show_bookings_invoice_id_fkey on delete set null (20260811120000_show_ops.sql ~278-299), so a soft-void is indeed straightforward.

findings.title: Invoice generation is non-atomic and race-prone — double-click or concurrent finance users can double-invoice a supplier
findings.spec_item: Reservations→Invoice (CRUCIAL)
findings.current_state: generateInvoicePackAction does read-then-three-writes with no transaction: query uninvoiced bookings (695-706), insert invoice (714-731), insert lines (747), then mark bookings (750-756). Two overlapping submissions (double-click on the plain HTML form at invoices/page.tsx:245 — the button is never disabled — or two finance users) both read invoice_id IS NULL and both create full invoices for the same reservations; the bookings' invoice_id ends up pointing at whichever ran last, but BOTH invoices with full totals exist → supplier billed twice. The final update also lacks an .is('invoice_id', null) guard, and if the line insert at 747 throws, an orphan invoice row with a non-zero total but no lines is left behind while the bookings remain uninvoiced — the retry then creates a duplicate.
findings.fix: Make it atomic and idempotent: move the whole operation into a single Postgres RPC (insert invoice, insert lines, and UPDATE show_bookings SET invoice_id=... WHERE invoice_id IS NULL, aborting/recalculating if the claimed row count differs from the preview). Minimum patch without an RPC: claim bookings first with the conditional update, then build the invoice only from successfully-claimed rows, and delete the invoice if line insert fails.
findings.verify_note: Verified line by line. generateInvoicePackAction: read (actions.ts:695-706) → insert invoice (714-731) → insert lines (747) → update bookings (750-756) with no transaction/RPC and no .is('invoice_id', null) guard on the final update. The generate form (invoices/page.tsx:245-283) is a plain server-action form in a server component — no pending state, button never disabled. The DB offers no cross-invoice protection: unique(invoice_id, booking_id) on show_invoice_lines (migration ~291) only dedupes within one invoice, so two overlapping runs both pass the null-check read and both commit full invoices for the same bookings. Orphan path also confirmed: a line-insert failure throws at 748 after the invoice row committed at 714 and before bookings are claimed at 750 — retry produces a duplicate invoice with a full total.

findings.title: Matty's headline ask is unbuilt: no invoice emails and no Stripe payment links on supplier invoices
findings.spec_item: Matty's additions: tracked Stripe payments for invoices; emails that send invoices with payment links
findings.current_state: The only email sender in the module is sendShowOpsPaymentLinkEmail (guest deposit-balance links). There is no send-invoice email, no way to attach/email the invoice pack to a supplier, and no Stripe checkout for supplier invoices — markInvoicePaidAction is a manual tick only. The config flag partner_stripe_enabled exists (config.ts:118, default false) but is consumed nowhere in the codebase (only copied through in actions.ts:172) — it is dead config. show_suppliers has no email/contact field in the schema, so there is nowhere to even send an invoice.
findings.fix: Add supplier contact email to show_suppliers + master UI; build sendSupplierInvoiceEmail rendering the pack (reuse invoices/[id] layout) with a Stripe Checkout link for total_amount on the connected account (metadata solvio_kind='show_ops_invoice', invoice id), extend the webhook to set paid/paid_at on completion, and gate it behind partner_stripe_enabled.
findings.verify_note: Verified. show-ops-emails.ts exports exactly one sender, sendShowOpsPaymentLinkEmail (guest deposit links). invoices/[id]/page.tsx has no send/email affordance (print + markInvoicePaidAction only). The Stripe webhook handles only solvio_kind 'show_ops_deposit' (api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:21 and 261) — no invoice kind exists anywhere. partner_stripe_enabled is parsed (config.ts:118, default false, also types.ts:50/69) and merely copied through in updateShowOpsOpsConfigAction (actions.ts:172); repo-wide grep confirms nothing consumes it — dead config. show_suppliers has no email/contact column (migration 20260811120000_show_ops.sql:95-108: name, partner_type, billing_mode, deposit_percent, invoice_nett_percent, notes, active only), so there is literally no address to send an invoice to.

findings.title: No over-payment guard and no way to void a mis-keyed payment
findings.spec_item: Payments tab: manually enter payments cash or card / flawless-system
findings.current_state: recordPaymentAction accepts any amount > 0 with no comparison against the outstanding balance (actions.ts:573-575). Typing 700 instead of 70 records €700: balance clamps to 0 (calc.ts:95 Math.max) and status flips to 'paid', so the over-collection is invisible in the UI and cash reconciliation can't spot it. There is no delete/void action for show_booking_payments anywhere (the only .delete() in actions.ts is for members, line 563) and negative amounts are rejected, so a mistake is permanent. The action also never checks billing_mode, so payments can be recorded against invoice-mode bookings (flipping their 'n_a' status) via Ops Brain or a crafted POST.
findings.fix: Reject or explicitly confirm amounts exceeding the current outstanding figure; reject invoice-mode bookings; add an office/finance-only voidPaymentAction (soft-delete with audit trail) that re-runs paymentStatusAfter.
findings.verify_note: Core confirmed: recordPaymentAction (actions.ts:573-575) accepts any amount > 0 with no comparison to outstanding balance; calc.ts:95 Math.max clamps balance to 0 so €700-for-€70 flips status to 'paid' and the over-collection is invisible outside the raw payments log; no delete/void action for show_booking_payments exists anywhere (only member delete, actions.ts:563) and negatives are rejected, so no compensating entry is possible. billing_mode is indeed never checked (booking select at 577-582 has no mode filter), so a payment against an invoice-mode booking would flip its 'n_a' status. ADJUSTMENT: the 'via Ops Brain' vector is factually wrong — brain-tools.ts exposes no payment-recording tool (only opsCountBookings, opsBusNeeds, opsFindBooking, opsListUnpaid, opsListProducts, opsListSuppliers, opsListHotels, opsCreateBooking). The invoice-mode vector requires a hand-crafted POST to the server action; the UI can't reach it (payments/page.tsx:44 filters billing_mode='deposit'). Severity major stands on the over-payment + no-void facts alone.

findings.title: Bookings can never be cancelled or deleted — cancelled guests keep flowing into payments-due and supplier invoices
findings.spec_item: flawless-system
findings.current_state: There is no delete-booking action and no cancelled status anywhere (grep across actions.ts, brain-tools.ts and types.ts shows the only delete is for members; payment_status enum is unpaid/partial/paid/n_a). When a guest cancels, the booking stays live: it appears on the Payments-due list demanding money, and if invoice-mode it WILL be swept into the next supplier pack (generateInvoicePackAction filters only billing_mode/invoice_id/date, actions.ts:695-704) and billed to the supplier. The only workaround is editing pax to 0, which leaves a €0 ghost line on invoices and pollutes stats.
findings.fix: Add a cancelled boolean/status with a cancel action (office+), exclude cancelled bookings from payments-due, invoice-pack queries, lists and outlook, and keep them visible (struck through) in Last 50 for audit.
findings.verify_note: Verified by repo-wide grep: no delete-booking or cancel action exists in actions.ts, brain-tools.ts, or any show-ops page; payment_status enum is exactly 'unpaid'|'partial'|'paid'|'n_a' (types.ts:170) with no cancelled state, and show_bookings has no cancelled/status column in the migration. A cancelled deposit-mode guest stays on Payments-due (payments/page.tsx:44-46 filters only mode+status) and a cancelled invoice-mode guest is swept into the next pack at full nett (generateInvoicePackAction filters only supplier/billing_mode/invoice_id/date, actions.ts:695-704). The pax-0 workaround checks out and is worse than stated: recompute at actions.ts:500 yields balance 0 but status 'unpaid' (paid=0), so the €0 ghost still appears on Payments-due as well as producing €0 invoice lines.

findings.title: Supplier invoice_nett_percent is silently ignored whenever product-level netts are set
findings.spec_item: Suppliers/partners: % for deposit calc or invoice nett rate
findings.current_state: adultNettUnit = Number(input.product?.adult_nett ?? adultPrice * nettPct) (calc.ts:23-24): if the product has adult_nett/child_nett filled in, the supplier's invoice_nett_percent is never applied — every supplier gets the identical product nett regardless of their negotiated rate. The master UI exposes BOTH fields with no precedence hint (master/page.tsx:90/132 supplier %, 165/202 product nett €), so MHT setting a product nett once would flatten all per-supplier deals; conversely a supplier % edit appears to do nothing on shows that have netts. This is the number that lands on Verifactu invoices.
findings.fix: Decide precedence explicitly and surface it: either apply the supplier % ON TOP of/instead of product nett with a clear rule, or per-supplier nett overrides. Minimum: compute nett as product nett × (invoice_nett_percent/100) or show 'supplier % ignored — product nett set' in both master forms.
findings.verify_note: Verified. calc.ts:23-24: adultNettUnit = Number(input.product?.adult_nett ?? adultPrice * nettPct) — the ?? means any non-null product nett bypasses the supplier % entirely (nettPct computed at calc.ts:21 then unused). upsertProductAction stores null when the field is blank (actions.ts:231-232), so the % only ever applies to products with empty netts. Master UI exposes both with no precedence hint: supplier 'Invoice nett %' at master/page.tsx:90 and 129-134, product 'Adult/Child nett €' at 165-166 and 202-203 — line cites accurate. The flattened nett lands directly on invoice totals (booking nett_total → generateInvoicePackAction sum at actions.ts:711). One could argue explicit-price-overrides-% is intended precedence, but it contradicts Joel's spec placing the nett rate on the supplier, and the silent interaction (a supplier % edit visibly doing nothing) is a real defect on Verifactu-bound figures. Major is defensible.

findings.title: Nett totals are frozen at booking-save time — later rate changes never reach the invoice
findings.spec_item: Reservations→Invoice / master data one-click editable
findings.current_state: nett/adult_nett/child_nett totals are computed only inside buildBookingFields at create/edit (actions.ts:361-367) and generateInvoicePackAction just sums the stored booking.nett_total (actions.ts:711). If Joel renegotiates a supplier's nett % mid-month, all existing uninvoiced bookings keep the old rate and the month-end pack mixes rates with no indication. Price-at-booking may be intended, but it is undocumented and invisible to the finance user.
findings.fix: Either recompute netts from current supplier/product rates at pack-generation time, or keep freeze-at-booking but state it in the generate UI ('nett rates as at time of booking') so finance knows which contract applies.

findings.title: Invoice list silently truncated to the latest 50 invoices
findings.spec_item: Invoice list report: all invoices w/ details
findings.current_state: The invoice list query has .limit(50) with no pagination or period filter; once MHT passes 50 invoices (a few months at their volume), older invoices — including unpaid ones — disappear from the list view entirely (they still show in Overdue only while unpaid). Lines are also only fetched for those 50.
findings.fix: Add pagination or a period filter to the list view and drop the silent cap; show a total count.

findings.title: Adult/child counts missing from invoice preview and print — supplier can't verify pax against the nett

findings.current_state: Joel's line spec reads as count + nett per bracket. show_invoice_lines stores adults/children and the preview query even selects them (invoices/page.tsx:73), but neither the preview table (invoices/page.tsx:221-239), the list drill-down (381-404), nor the printable invoice ([id]/page.tsx — the select at line 26-28 omits adults/children entirely) displays the counts. findings.title: Currency hardcoded as € across all invoice screens, and amounts rendered without 2-dp formatting
findings.spec_item: flawless-system (white-label module supports eur/gbp/usd)

findings.title: Stripe webhook records the payment without checking session.payment_status and ignores async payment events
findings.spec_item: Matty's additions: tracked Stripe payments
findings.current_state: markShowOpsDepositPaid applies the payment on checkout.session.completed without checking session.payment_status === 'paid' (route.ts:20-36). findings.fix: Guard with if (session.payment_status !== 'paid') return; add async_payment_succeeded (apply payment) and async_payment_failed (notify/flag) cases, or pin payment_method_types: ['card'] in createShowOpsDepositCheckoutSession.

findings.title: Payments page show-filter dropdown ignores the island filter

findings.title: No export/download for any commercial report — Joel cannot get these into Google Sheets

findings.title: No per-partner-per-show matrix — spec's core 'tab per partner type' deliverable is aggregates only

findings.title: 'Nightly tracker' has no per-night LY/LM/LW comparison, and the 'last week' window is wrong
findings.spec_item: 'nightly tracker vs LY vs LM vs LW'
findings.current_state: The comparisons are month-level aggregates, not nightly: monthPax() (lines 133-148) returns whole-month pax for LM and LY, and the per-night bar list (lines 274-290) shows current-month nights only with no comparison series. Worse, the 'last week window' is defined as the 7 days ending the day before the 1st of the selected month (lines 150-154) — viewing August on Aug 12 compares against Jul 25-31, which is not 'last week' by any reading, and that 7-day pax is displayed next to a full-month total (line 267) with no like-for-like normalization, so the number is meaningless.
findings.fix: Make the tracker genuinely nightly: for each show night, fetch same-date-last-year, same-date-last-month, and same-weekday-last-week pax and render them as comparison columns/bars per night. If a month-summary LW figure is kept, define it as the 7 days ending today (or the last 7 days of the selected month) and compare against the equivalent 7-day window, not the month total.

findings.title: Year-on-year tracker is structurally zero — no way to import historical bookings
